- Model consistently overestimates prices in the early part of the forecast horizon, especially after sharp spikes or volatility events.
- Forecasts tend to be too high in the first 5–10 days post-forecast, then gradually correct — suggesting a lag in adjusting to true market dynamics.
- After a significant price spike, model often overshoots and fails to account for subsequent mean reversion or downward correction.
- Model underestimates prices during prolonged downward trends or when historical mean is lower than recent highs.
- Forecasts show persistent bias toward higher values when recent history includes high volatility or sharp corrections — model fails to capture “reset” or “rebound” phases.
- Model exhibits poor sensitivity to sudden drops in price — often fails to recognize sharp downward corrections in the first 3–5 days.
- Forecasts are overly smooth — fail to capture short-term volatility or sudden reversals, especially in the last 5–10 days of the forecast window.
- Model tends to overfit recent high values, leading to persistent overestimation when true price is trending downward or consolidating.
